title: test(spec): order the sdui cleanup fd count on the child's own post-exec report
body:
Fixes #18010

Clause-②: no — the diff is one `.test.ts` under `packages/spec/scripts/`, which matches none of the package's `files[]` entries.

## The mechanism, named from the tree

The card's hypothesis was that the count lags the child's exit (an fd inherited by a grandchild, or a lock fd closed asynchronously). **Both halves are falsified by the tree**, and the real cause is one line earlier:

- The count is **not** taken after the child exits. It is deliberately taken while the session leader is alive (the comment at the old `:98-102`), and the failing CI run confirms it: `LEADER_ALIVE_AT_COUNT=yes`.
- No grandchild can hold the fd. Measured here: a node process holding an inherited non-close-on-exec fd reports `PARENT_SELF_LOCKFDS=1`, and the child it spawns reports `HELPER_LOCKFDS=0`. libuv closes it across the spawn, so the helper is not a candidate.

What is left is the only candidate, and it is the one the test synchronises on:

`sdui_spawn_detached` (`scripts/gen-sdui-manifest.sh:88`) returns as soon as the pidfile is non-empty (`:113-115`). Its runner writes that pid on its **first** line (`:96`), **before** the `for fd in /proc/$$/fd/*` loop that closes the descriptors inherited from the caller (`:98-105`), and only then `exec`s. So between those two steps the session leader is a `bash` process that is published as ready **and still holds the caller's flock descriptor**. That is precisely what `Test Core (1/6)` counted.

Measured on this tree, 25 runs, timestamps taken with bash's `EPOCHREALTIME` inside an instrumented copy of the script:

| reading | value |
|---|---|
| window, pid published to descriptors closed | 151–297 us (median 174) |
| margin, descriptors closed minus count taken | 10.4–54.3 ms, all 25 negative (the close won) |
| what buys that margin | `sdui_spawn_detached`'s own `sleep 0.05` poll granularity (`:117`) — not a barrier |

So the assertion was ordered on a signal that means "the leader exists", never "the leader let go of my descriptors", and a 0.2 ms critical section was being covered by an unrelated 50 ms sleep. On a six-way sharded runner a single `bash` process being descheduled for longer than that is ordinary. **The assertion was racing something real; it was not wrong about the property.**

## What changed

The reading is now ordered on the resource, not on the pidfile:

1. **Barrier 1 — the spawned command's own post-exec report.** The stub counts its own descriptors on the caller's lock and prints them. `exec` has by then replaced the shell that does the closing, so that line cannot exist until the close has run. The harness waits for the **report**, never for a value: the stub prints whatever it counts, so a real leak still arrives as a red (proved below).
2. **Barrier 2 — the helper has joined the session**, so the session-wide count covers both members rather than whoever happened to exist.
3. The session-wide `LOCKFDS` count is unchanged in meaning and now runs after both barriers, and names its holders (`LOCKFD_HOLDERS`) so a future red is a process rather than a number.
4. The stub is released by a file instead of a 1200 ms timer, so `LEADER_ALIVE_AT_COUNT` stops racing node's boot time — the added barriers would otherwise have eaten into that budget.
5. The orphan precondition waits for a member with PPID 1 instead of sleeping a guessed two seconds. A timed-out barrier leaves the field empty, which the existing assertion reads as a red.

Both new barriers are asserted (`CHILD_REPORTED`, `HELPER_IN_SESSION`), so a barrier that times out is its own named failure instead of a count taken at some other moment.

⛔ Nothing was skipped, quarantined, loosened to `toBeLessThan`, retry-wrapped, or given a longer timeout. The vitest timeout is still `120_000`.

## Ablations — one-time, on the real script, restored and proved byte-identical

Both legs mutate `scripts/gen-sdui-manifest.sh` in this worktree only, under `trap ... EXIT INT TERM`, restore with `git checkout HEAD -- ...`, and verify `git hash-object` against the HEAD blob.

**(1) The lagging state — the OLD assertion fails on it, the NEW one passes.** A `sleep 0.5` injected between the pid publish and the fd-close loop, i.e. the deschedule made deterministic:

| leg | result |
|---|---|
| NEW test under the lag | `exit 0`, `Tests 1 passed (1)` |
| OLD test (BASE `2882528786` content) under the **same** lag | `exit 1` — `LOCKFDS=2`, `LEADER_ALIVE_AT_COUNT=yes`, `expected '2' to be '0'` |

The CI red read `'1'`; this reads `'2'` because the injected `sleep` is itself a session member that inherited the same descriptor — an artefact of the injection, not of the script.

**(2) Non-vacuity — the NEW assertion still fails when the thing it pins is deleted.** The fd hygiene disabled (`if [ -d "/proc/$$/fd" ]; then` to `if false; then`):

```
ABL_2_EXIT=1
CHILD_REPORTED=yes
CHILD_LOCKFDS=1
HELPER_IN_SESSION=yes
LOCKFDS=1
LOCKFD_HOLDERS=[ 28876(node)]
: expected '1' to be '0'
```

The holder is the exec'd `node` leader — the process that can actually survive cleanup, which is what property (2) exists to pin. Both barriers reported `yes`, so the red is the property, not a barrier artefact.

Restore proof for both legs: `RESTORED rel=scripts/gen-sdui-manifest.sh blob=5233551907c06460756c91d061e2078276e42ca1` equal to `HEAD:scripts/gen-sdui-manifest.sh`, and `RESTORE_DIFF_HEAD=[]`.

## Verification

Exit codes captured by redirect-then-`$?`, never through a pipe.

- Subject test, clean tree: **5 consecutive runs, all `exit 0`**, 1.71–2.91 s (was 4.47 s on BASE — the blind `sleep 2` is gone).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test:repo` — `exit 0`, 31 files / 526 tests. This is the project and the shard that failed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` (local project) — `exit 0`, 482 files / 13771 tests, 1 skipped.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` — `exit 0`; `check:test-typecheck` confirms the test layer compiles under `packages/spec/tsconfig.test.json`, so this file is in a tsc program.
- Gate family from `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`: **58 derived, 58 accounted, 0 UNRUN — 53 `exit 0`, 5 `exit 3`**. The five are `check:dts-closure`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check:sourcemap-no-sources-content`, `check:type-check-debt`: all refuse for a missing built `dist/` in this worktree. **PREREQUISITE NOT MET — not measured, neither a pass nor a failure.** They sweep published build output, which this diff cannot reach; CI's Build Core job supplies it.

**Verify-lock confounder, ruled out by measurement rather than assertion.** This test counts flock descriptors, so a lock-holding wrapper around it is a confounder. Running the probe inside `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`: `SESSION_VERIFYLOCK_FDS=0` and `CALLER_VERIFYLOCK_FDS=0` — the shared lock's descriptor is not in the wrapped tree at all. Lit control on the same grep: a process deliberately holding `/tmp/os-heavy-verify.lock` reads `1`, so those zeros are facts, not a broken probe. The count itself greps the test's own `caller.lock` basename, which the shared lock's name cannot match; dark control `LOCKFDS_DARK=0`, lit control `CALLER_LOCKFDS_LIT=1`.

## skip-changeset

Measured, not assumed: `npm pack --dry-run --json` in `packages/spec` lists **271 entries, 0 of them under `scripts/`**, and the subject file is not among them. Positive control: `README.md`, `llms.txt` and `package.json` are in that listing, so it is a real reading. Nothing published moves.

## Acceptance notes

Out of scope for this PR, noted and not filed:

- `sdui_spawn_detached` publishes the leader pid before it closes the caller's descriptors, so the pidfile means less than its own doc comment claims ("no inherited descriptors above stderr"). It is not a production defect — the pre-exec shell always proceeds to the close, and nothing in the script reads the leader's descriptors — so the honest fix is the measurement point, not the script. Recorded because the next author to treat that pidfile as a readiness barrier will hit the same thing. Carrier: any future change to `sdui_spawn_detached`.
- The old orphan scan (`for p in $MEMBERS; do [ ... ] && ORPHAN="$p"; done`) relies on `set -e`'s `&&`-list exemption and would abort the harness if a non-orphan member were scanned last. It only ever passed because the session holds exactly one member and that member is the orphan. Rewritten as an `if` here as part of the barrier change. Carrier: this file.

## Landing note (seat, 2026-09-17)

Contract review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on head `65c97a0760`: **PASS** — record is comment `5706854237` on this PR.

⚠️ **Correction to this body, appended rather than rewritten.** The body attributes this file's tsc coverage to `check:test-typecheck` under `tsconfig.test.json`. That program's `include` stops at `src/**/*`, so it does not reach `packages/spec/scripts/`. The file is compiled by `check:scripts-typecheck` under `tsconfig.scripts.json` (`include: scripts/**/*`), which `typecheck` also runs and which is green on this head. **The conclusion holds — the file IS in a tsc program — but the attribution named the wrong one.** Corrected here because this repo squashes and the body becomes the permanent commit message on `main`.

**What the review checked that the seat specifically asked it to be sceptical about:** whether the reordering makes the assertion deterministic or merely makes the flake rarer. It concluded deterministic **by program order, not by timing**: the count cannot begin until `EXECED=1` is visible, that line is written by `node`, `node` exists only after `exec` at script :104, and the fd-close loop at :96–103 precedes that `exec` in the same process. A barrier that never arrives reds by name (`CHILD_REPORTED=no`) — it never passes. All eight original assertions survive with identical matchers; no retry, no loosened matcher, no lengthened sleep, no skip.

**Pre-landing checks:** ① review PASS on record ✅ · ② `check-clause2-carriers --pair 18530` exit 0; ⛔ no carriers were hung on this pair (`Clause-②: no`, no contract surface) so there is nothing to strip ✅ · ③ re-taken at landing time, latest-run-per-check-name ✅. Governed-surface predicate: **0 of 1 path hits the register** ⇒ ordinary queue landing.
